title: Pricing by hours per project for residential cleaning
audience: Solo residential cleaners and owners of small house-cleaning crews who write quotes for regular and deep cleans and need a price that covers cost and earns a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for a house clean
instruction.body: A house clean is mostly time: the hours on site, the trip to the home, set-up, pack-down and a checking pass. Start from hours so that each quote shows its cost, its margin and the effect of a scope change. Marketplace hourly figures are references, not your costs, so they cannot replace the calculation.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's total business costs by chargeable hours, not paid hours. Total costs include wages with on-costs where you employ staff, plus vehicle running costs, chemicals and cloths, equipment, insurance and admin. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Xero Australia advises dividing by billable hours rather than total hours (3 September 2026). Jobber's cleaning guide says cleaners often undercount on-costs, which it puts at 25 to 40 per cent of wages. That guide is US-leaning, so its percentage is not an Australian rate. Gap: the research has no Australian figure for cleaner on-costs.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours for each home
instruction.body: Break the home into rooms and tasks, estimate each at a standard speed from your own timed cleans, and add set-up, pack-down, travel and checking as named lines. Use a range where the home is unknown, for example a home with pets or heavy build-up. Add a set allowance for delays such as late access. Xero Australia suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work, which is the source's own range and not a cleaning benchmark. After each clean, record the actual hours and the reason for any difference.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then add a margin that reflects your target and the risk in the job, such as difficult access or a long drive. Apply your minimum charge. The result is a price with a visible basis. The marketplace figure for a three-bedroom home ($140 an hour, Airtasker, 27 August 2025) is a comparison point. It is for cleaning time and does not include travel or checking, so it does not compare directly with a price built from all the hours.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A quote states the rooms and tasks, the hours basis, exclusions (for example, the inside of appliances), what the household must provide (access, pets, what is cleared), and how long the quote is valid. Price any extra work in writing before it is done. Business Queensland suggests charging unplanned extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage; it suggests 15 per cent, which is a suggestion and not a benchmark.

instruction.heading: Review your estimates
instruction.body: Compare estimated and actual hours for each home type until the variance settles. If the gap stays large, change the standard time, the margin or the scope rules. A method is finished only when actual hours match quoted hours closely enough for the work to make money.

procedure: Gather the year's total business costs and the chargeable hours for the same period, with a source for each figure.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours to get the cost per productive hour, and date the result.
Break the home into rooms and tasks, and estimate each as a range from your own timed cleans.
Add set-up, pack-down, travel and checking time as named lines.
Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then apply the margin for access, pets or build-up.
Apply your minimum charge, and state whether GST is included.
Write the quote with scope, hours basis, exclusions, household inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each clean and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: A solo cleaner quotes a fortnightly regular clean for a three-bedroom house (illustrative). Estimated time on site is 3.0 hours, with 0.25 hours for set-up and pack-down, 0.5 hours of travel and 0.25 hours of checking (all illustrative). The cost per productive hour is $55 (illustrative; not a sourced figure). The target margin is 25 per cent of price (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost of the clean, what is the price, and how does the marketplace reference compare?
workedExamples.reasoning: Crew hours are 3.0 + 0.25 + 0.5 + 0.25, which is 4.0. The cost is 4.0 x $55, which is $220.00 (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which gives $293.33 (CALC). The Airtasker reference for a three-bedroom home is $140 an hour, which would be $420 for three hours (vendor, 27 August 2025). That reference is for cleaning time and excludes travel and checking, so the cleaner states the basis on the quote. Floor check: the Level 1 adult minimum in the Cleaning Services Award is $25.85 an hour, and with 25 per cent casual loading it is $32.31 an hour (Fair Work Commission; variation from 1 July 2025; 2026-27 rates not checked). That floor excludes super, leave, insurance and vehicle costs, so it is not the cost per hour.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for area estimates

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Dividing costs by paid hours rather than chargeable hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026).

commonErrors.error: Leaving out travel between homes, set-up and checking time.
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate, so a short clean with a long drive is priced honestly.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no exclusions or access terms.
commonErrors.prevention: List pets, access, what the household clears and the items excluded, such as inside appliances.

commonErrors.error: Matching the marketplace hourly figure without costing the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Compare the reference with your own hours and cost, and say which one the quote uses.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to price statements, and the ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State and territory fair trading rules differ, so check the rules for your state.

Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award (MA000022) may set their minimum rates. The Level 1 adult minimum was $25.85 an hour from 1 July 2025, with a 25 per cent casual loading. The research did not check the 2026-27 rates, so confirm the current award before you use any cost figure.
The research did not confirm how leave and super are treated for a sole trader. Check this with a registered tax agent before you publish a rate.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten jobs of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Start every house quote from measured hours and a cost per chargeable hour.
Name travel, set-up and checking time, and state exclusions and access in writing.
Gaps: cleaner on-cost rates, the 2026-27 award rates and a residential minimum charge were not confirmed. Check them before you use a figure.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in a house cleaner's cost per productive hour?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker
The price the household pays, plus any deposit taken
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin, divided by chargeable hours
The marketplace rate for three-bedroom homes

knowledgeChecks.question: A house clean is estimated at 4 crew-hours and takes 5.5. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate alone, because the household has paid
Cut the crew's breaks on the next clean
Raise the price for this household only and change nothing else

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a home quote need an exclusions list?
options: To show what the price covers, so extra work can be priced before it is done
To make the quote longer for the household
To hide the margin from the household
To lower the household's expectations of the result

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours, not total hours; add a set allowance for delays; the guide's 10 to 20 per cent range for unexpected work is the source's own figure.

Jobber Academy, 'How Much to Charge for House Cleaning', https://getjobber.com/academy/cleaning/how-much-to-charge-for-house-cleaning/, 31 March 2026 (first published June 2023). US-leaning source. Supports: cleaners often undercount on-costs such as payroll tax, workers' compensation and unpaid travel, which the source puts at 25 to 40 per cent of wages; a profit factor on cost; annual price reviews; a flat or minimum-hours charge for short cleaning jobs.

Airtasker, 'Airbnb cleaning service cost', https://www.airtasker.com/au/costs/airbnb-cleaning/airbnb-cleaning-service-cost, last updated 27 August 2025. Vendor marketplace; the house-cleaning page could not be read. Supports: hourly rates by bedroom count, per-room prices, a regular clean range of $80 to $180, and a guest fee range of $50 to $300 per booking.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Queensland. Supports: list add-ons and alternatives on the quote; charge extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage (the source suggests 15 per cent, which is not a benchmark); follow up 7 to 14 days after the quote; confirm scope, capacity and deadline before quoting.

business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost plus a margin.

Notes: $55 an hour, the hours and the 25 per cent margin are illustrative and are not sourced. $25.85 and $32.31 are from the Cleaning Services Award figures in the research file, with $32.31 calculated as $25.85 x 1.25.
